summary: SCIM attribute 'employeeType' misclassification marks svc-bot as 'temp', blocking Analytics Console RBAC
description:
Issue summary:
A service account (svc-analytics-bot@redwood.com) was provisioned by the SCIM bridge with employeeType="temp" due to a recent identity-sync rule. That attribute value prevents automatic group assignment for the "analytics-read" RBAC role, resulting in 403s when the bot attempts to access the Analytics Console API.

Impact:
- Automated ingestion and dashboard refresh jobs from the analytics bot are failing (403 Forbidden).
- Multiple downstream jobs that rely on fresh metrics are delayed (data freshness impacted).
- Incident risk for customer-facing dashboards if bot cannot be restored.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) 
- Affected principal: svc-analytics-bot@redwood.com (service account)
- Identity sync component: identity-provisioner (SCIM bridge v1.9.2) talking to Okta

Steps to reproduce:
1) Create or update an account with email containing "-bot" (e.g., svc-analytics-bot@redwood.com) in Okta
2) Trigger SCIM provisioning (fk-provision job) or wait for next scheduled sync
3) Observe generated SCIM PATCH payload and resulting user resource in identity DB
4) Check group assignment service: attribute employeeType is evaluated for RBAC rule engine
5) Attempt to call Analytics Console API with service account token -> 403 returned

Observed behavior:
- SCIM bridge sets employeeType="temp" for this service account due to a newly deployed provisioning rule that maps non-corporate domains and certain naming patterns to "temp".
- RBAC engine rejects auto-assignment to analytics groups for employeeType="temp".
- System logs show: "rbac: deny auto-group assignment - employeeType=temp" and Analytics Console returns "403: missing analytics-read role".

Expected behavior:
- Service accounts created for internal automation should be exempt from the employeeType->RBAC exclusion or be tagged with employeeType="service" so the analytics-read role applies.

Logs / traces:
- Okta System Log (2026-03-10T02:14:38Z): eventId=00u8Xf12 - SCIM push for user svc-analytics-bot@redwood.com
- identity-provisioner (fk-provision) trace: provisioning.request.id=prov-9a3c, payload contained employeeType="temp" (rule: mapDomainToTemp v2.3)
- RBAC service log (2026-03-10T02:14:42Z): rbac-eval requestId=rbac-44f - decision=deny, reason=employeeType=temp
- Analytics Console access log: 2026-03-10T02:14:43Z svc-analytics-bot 403 GET /api/v1/ingest

Investigation notes:
- On 2026-03-09 we merged a change (see PR) to identity-provisioner: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-provisioner/pull/418 which tightened mapping rules to label certain domains as "temp". The rule inadvertently matched email localparts containing "-bot" via a regex intended for contractor emails.
- Confirmed behavior by replaying provisioning payloads in staging and reproducing the employeeType mapping.
- Checked historical provisioning: svc-analytics-bot had employeeType="service" before the PR; change correlates with introduction of mapDomainToTemp v2.3.
- No prior alerts triggered because most service bots are exempted at the group-assignment layer, but analytics bot was not on the exemption list.

Workaround applied:
- Manual group assignment: Support assigned svc-analytics-bot to "analytics-read" group via Admin Console at 2026-03-10T03:10Z to restore immediate access.
- Rolled back automated rule in identity-provisioner by temporarily pinning mapping config to v2.2 (hotfix) to stop new misclassifications while we prepare a permanent fix.

Proposed fix / next steps:
1) Patch identity-provisioner mapping rule to exclude service accounts by checking attribute isServiceAccount=true or by matching an explicit allowlist for known svc-* accounts. (owner: identity team, ETA: 2026-03-12)
2) Add a unit+integration test for the regex to prevent matching "-bot" localparts. (owner: identity team, ETA: 2026-03-12)
3) Add a fallback in RBAC auto-group-assignment: if account email matches svc- prefix, treat as "service" unless explicitly classified as contractor. (owner: platforms team, ETA: 2026-03-20)
4) Reconcile and retroactively fix any other service accounts mis-tagged by running a one-off migration script (owner: identity ops, ETA: 2026-03-14)

Follow-ups / action items:
- Update runbook to include checks for service account mappings after provisioning rule changes.
- Produce a short postmortem summarizing root cause and timeline once fully resolved.

Related artifacts:
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-provisioner/pull/418
- Hotfix: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-provisioner/commit/8a7f6b2
